phrases.latin: Quae dum loquuntur, cornīx ālīs plaudēns āvolāvit.
phrases.english: While they were talking, the crow flapped its wings and flew away.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 141, checked against the searchable text of the book on 29 October 2026.: p. 316.

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
